postmortem.hypothesis: Select Y and phi, whose reference excursions dominate; X compensation remains zero. The latest deterioration is principally phi, not X. Redesign the phase logic to preserve rising and holding drive, suppress premature phi descent, and unload Y only during its commanded return. Applied-output inconsistencies prevent treating this lap as a clean test of the reported class.
postmortem.design_strategy: Use subtraction-only, phase-conditioned feedback with filtered velocity, continuous dead zones, bounded residuals, and direct residual slew limiting. Unlike the previous controller, Y receives no damping reduction during ascent or dwell. Its return unloading depends on predicted tracking error, and relaxes when measured descent catches the reference. Phi positive-side braking requires near-target predicted overshoot; negative-side suppression gives current position error priority over reference-velocity demand, preventing early descent while phi is already below reference. No integral, pressure threshold, precharge, clock-indexed replay, or antagonist activation is introduced. With the supplied pair-exclusive MPC commands and fixed break-before-make planner, subtraction cannot create simultaneous positive antagonist drive. Unlock immediately clears channel output, as required. Source was manually audited against the executable contract; no files or hardware were accessed.

postmortem.designer_failure_analysis: Relative to the stable lap, squared axis RMSE changes are approximately X −7.01, Y +5.82, and phi +16.74 deg², explaining the aggregate +15.55 deterioration. Y still has a repeated charging deficit at 2.35–3.5 s, then loses height during phi motion: approximately 33.4 degrees at 6.85 s to 22.6 degrees near 10 s. The previous subtraction-only law could not restore that deficit. Its final-return objective partly succeeded: final mean error magnitude is now 3.791 degrees, although the requested final-phase RMSE is not supplied. Phi still charges late, accelerates to about 33 deg/s, then falls prematurely during the upper dwell; its downward-phase improvement objective failed. Crucially, the trace contains positive V3 compensation up to 420 mV during dwell and simultaneous positive V2/V3 totals, although the tested class cannot return positive residuals. At 8.75 s even V2 has a positive residual with zero base command. These observations indicate additional actuation processing or a report

Its final-return objective partly succeeded: final mean error magnitude is now 3.791 degrees, although the requested final-phase RMSE is not supplied. Crucially, the trace contains positive V3 compensation up to 420 mV during dwell and simultaneous positive V2/V3 totals, although the tested class cannot return positive residuals. These observations indicate additional actuation processing or a reporting mismatch; the deterioration cannot be attributed solely to the reported class. This replacement does not reproduce those additions and cannot cancel an unknown downstream override. Removing velocity-only ascent/holding reductions and prioritizing position during phi descent are testable changes, but unchanged charging authority remains a limitation.

design_memory_last_5.hypothesis: Select Y and phi: their commanded excursions dominate the reference and their baseline RMSEs are 6.9877 and 4.0391 degrees. X remains uncompensated. Start conservatively with signed voltage reductions: Y retains positive drive during its delayed return, while phi catches up rapidly and subsequently overshoots. The legacy phi antagonist precharge is incompatible with the stated hard rule and is not reproduced.
design_memory_last_5.design_strategy: Use bounded, subtraction-only proportional and velocity-error feedback on each existing MPC-driven side. A continuous dead zone reduces noise sensitivity; velocity error anticipates overshoot. Additional Y reference-velocity unloading addresses its delayed downward return without energizing the unavailable V1 channel. Corrections cannot create positive drive, increase electrical demand, or initiate an antagonist handoff; they preserve the fixed MPC/planner's break-before-make sequence. The supplied MPC base commands are pair-exclusive, even where legacy total commands were not. No integral, pressure threshold, time-indexed replay, or learned X correction is used. Residual slew is enforced directly, with the explicitly required immediate zero/reset on unlock. Negative residuals may exceed the instantaneous base magnitude; the specified lower clipping then gives zero voltage without requiring an abrupt residual reset.
design_memory_last_5.expected_effect: Next-lap hypotheses: reduce Y final-phase RMSE from 10.508 to below 9.5 degrees and absolute final mean error from 9.507 to below 8.5 degrees; reduce phi downward-motion tracking lead around 10.25–10.55 s and upper-dwell overshoot without repeated reversals. Target whole-lap MSE below 76.047 deg² while keeping maximum pose jump at or below 2.711 degrees. These are experimental targets, not predictions established by simulation. design_memory_last_5.designer_failure_analysis: First round: no previous proposed-controller result exists. Baseline Y remains nearly stationary until approximately 2.5 s, then accelerates sharply; late positive V0 commands also oppose unloading. Phi shows delayed onset followed by approximately 30 deg/s catch-up and substantial downward tracking lead. Baseline legacy outputs simultaneously energize V2 and V3 during precharge/handoff, so those behaviors cannot be retained despite the stable-baseline label. Subtraction-only control avoids introducing that conflict and needs no unverified pressure-to-force model. Its limitations are unchanged initial charging authority, possible loss of holding pressure, and potentially slower phi reversal after removing legacy precharge. Closed-loop improvement and repeatability require the next measured lap; source was self-audited but not executed on hardware.
